brief: Deutsche Bank reports a divergent session. In Europe, front-month natural gas closed at 73.60 euros per MWh, its highest since January 2023, on scepticism that Strait of Hormuz flows normalise soon and on Northern European reserves that are hard to refill before the heating season. Sustained high gas prices, with headline and core inflation still above target, raised fears of a more forceful ECB, and markets fully priced three more ECB hikes by June 2027. That pushed the 10yr bund to 3.37% and France's 10yr OAT to 4.25%, with German real yields also at post-2011 highs, so the move was not only inflation expectations. In the US, oil reversed from a peak above 97 dollars per barrel, letting Treasuries stabilise, and a softer ADP print of +38k against +47k expected cut September Fed hike pricing from 68% to 63%, with Williams sounding dovish. The S&P 500 rose 0.46% after three declines. Asia gained on Broadcom's chip-sales outlook. The yen rose after Takata said a 25bp hike is not set in stone, plus intervention chatter, easing 10yr JGBs to 2.97%. The Bank of Canada held at 2.25% but was read hawkishly.
